newsitem.title: INDIA: India to ease rules in mineral sector - minister.
newsitem.headline: India to ease rules in mineral sector - minister.

text.p: India on Thursday announced that all proposals for foreign equity investment in the mineral sector would be cleared on a case by case basis.
It would also soon decide on automatic approval for investment up to 50 percent of foreign equity participation in domestic mining sector.

"All proposals for foreign equity investment would be cleared through the FIPB (Foreign Investment Promotion Board) route on a case to case basis," Mines minister, Birendra Prasad Baishya told reporters.

"We would like to ordinarily limit automatic approval for foreign investment to 50 percent in the mineral sector but we are taking into account the views of the ministry of industry and other concerend ministries," Baishya said.
He said the government would soon take a final decision on the issue.
India, as part of a policy of economic liberalisation, in 1993 opened up 13 minerals previously reserved exclusively for the state sector.
It also invited private investment and greater participation in the mining sector.
Baishya said government would take special care in clearing projects for prospecting and mining of sensitive minerals like gold and diamonds.
He said the government had also framed new guidelines for companies to undertake mining in area beyond 25 square kms.

Under the new guidelines the government would consider the requests of the various state governments for prospecting licences beyond the existing ceiling of 25 square kms only if the company seeking licences agreed to carry out aerial prospecting.

It said the recommendations made by the state governments should not exceed 5,000 sq kms for a single prospecting licence. The total aggregate area held by one single company should not exceed 10,000 sq kms, a mining ministry statement said.
